scenarios: 6 developer-authored fictional claims, reused in previous development

arms.name: GPT + verification
arms.note: GPT extracts and an independent verifier controls the route.

arms.name: GPT + Jev
arms.note: Jev can escalate a case but cannot clear a mandatory safety review.

arms.name: Jev first
arms.note: Replayed selective GPT calling: all six Jev scores were ≥0.5, so nothing was skipped. C is a counterfactual, not a separate deployment.

cases.name: Water damage
cases.learning: GPT's evidence quotation did not pass literal verification, so the system stopped.

cases.name: Bicycle theft
cases.learning: Matching frame numbers. Jev nevertheless crossed the exploratory review threshold: unnecessary escalation.

cases.name: Liability
cases.learning: Conflicting liability statements need human judgment.

cases.name: Phone repair
cases.learning: Invoice amount conflicts with customer request.

cases.name: Suspicious document
cases.learning: A mandatory independent instruction-in-document guard escalated this case.

caveats: All examples were developer-authored, reused from earlier model development. Not blind or expert-labelled.
A/B outcomes derived from the same six real GPT and six real Jev API results; C is a conservative conditional counterfactual.
Times are observed individual API durations combined serially, not total operational processing times.
Costs apply published rate-card prices to recorded tokens, not billed invoices.
Reviewer effort, time and real claim completion cost were not measured.
A correctly verified result does not mean insurance coverage was determined. No payouts or customer actions.
Jev's 0.5 attention cutoff is exploratory, not validated or calibrated; zero critical continuation misses on a six-case authored suite cannot prove reliability.
